sub_indicators.label: Digital links and facilities shared with other African countries
sub_indicators.subject: gov.regional
sub_indicators.text: Shared regional infrastructure: digital links and facilities shared with other African countries
sub_indicators.norm_short: The African Union's Programme for Infrastructure Development in Africa and its Digital Transformation Strategy ask states to join their networks across borders, give landlocked countries a route to the sea cables and share exchange points and data centres.
criteria: A source from the past three years says the country shares no digital infrastructure with another African country.

In the past three years the country has agreed with another African country, or through a regional body, to build, join or jointly run shared digital infrastructure: a cross-border link, a shared internet exchange or shared data storage. Talks, a study or a bid to host do not count.
Building has started in the past three years: a contract awarded, works begun or cable being laid. A tender or money promised does not count.

One kind of shared infrastructure is in service under an arrangement both countries are party to: a link, a traffic exchange or data storage. A cable that only crosses or lands in the country, one company's network, or foreign networks joining its exchange, does not count.
Two of the three kinds, links, traffic exchange and data storage, are in service under such arrangements.
